field.label: Enable
field.help: Give devices that appear for the first time in the DHCP pool a temporary internet access window (Dnsmasq DHCP required).

field.label: Interface
field.help: Interface the new devices are connected to, typically a dedicated IoT network.

field.label: Pool start
field.help: First address of the dynamic DHCP range. Only leases inside the pool are considered, reserved addresses outside of it never get a window.

field.label: Pool end
field.help: Last address of the dynamic DHCP range.

field.label: Duration (minutes)
field.help: How long a newly seen device may reach the internet.

field.label: Excluded networks
field.help: Destinations that stay blocked during the window (internal networks).

field.label: Kill states on close
field.help: Drop open connections of the device when its window closes.

field.label: Log
field.help: Log traffic passed by the setup rule in the firewall log.

field.label: IPv4 alias
field.help: Existing host alias referenced by your firewall rule that grants permanent IPv4 internet access. The plugin adds and removes reserved addresses here. Leave empty to disable permanent access management.

field.label: MAC alias
field.help: Existing MAC alias referenced by your firewall rule for (IPv6) internet access. The plugin adds and removes MAC addresses here.

field.label: Reservation range start
field.help: Permanent devices get a fixed Dnsmasq DHCP reservation. The next free address in this range is used. Keep the range outside of the dynamic pool.

field.label: Reservation domain
field.help: Optional domain of new reservations (device name becomes host.domain).
